name: Ship.com
summary: Shipping software for online sellers: UPS and USPS labels at discounted rates, order tracking emails, marketing emails and a rewards program, with an AI assistant that prepares labels.
best_for: small online sellers who ship US parcels with UPS or USPS and want one tool for labels, tracking emails and basic marketing emails, and who ship enough to make a cap on shipments matter
skip_if: you ship mostly outside the US, you need carriers other than UPS and USPS, or you want a product we have tested ourselves instead of one read from its public pages
honest_knock: Starter is capped at 10 shipments a month and Growth at 100. Postage is billed on top of every plan, the pricing page shows no postage rates, and it names only UPS and USPS. The free shipping calculator does show them without an account: in our test on 18 November 2026, 2 lb from 10001 to 94105 came back at $10.15 for USPS Ground Advantage against $19.80 retail. The 'up to 89% off' line is a ceiling; the discounts we saw ran from 11% to 80%. Buying a label needs an account. The 30-day refund promise is limited to first-time customers with active order history.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · Starter $4.99 a month (monthly billing only, up to 10 shipments a month)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-12 on ship.com/pricing, US dollars) Ship.com sells four plans, and you pay postage on top of every one. Starter costs $4.99 a month, is sold monthly only and covers up to 10 shipments a month, discounted rates, email support and one platform integration. Growth costs $19.99 a month, or $14 a month on the yearly toggle, and covers up to 100 shipments a month, heavily discounted rates, priority email support, up to 1,000 marketing emails a month, batch shipping and printing and carrier pickup requests. Executive costs $29.99 a month, or $22 a month on the yearly toggle, and covers unlimited shipments, rates the page says are up to 89% off retail, live chat and phone support, up to 25,000 marketing emails a month, up to 3 platform integrations, a customer rewards program and business reporting. Enterprise has no listed price and adds a dedicated shipping account manager and API or custom integration work. The page offers a free 30-day trial of Executive with no credit card and says you pay only postage during it; Starter and Growth show a free trial of 2 shipments, also postage only. The page promises a refund of subscription fees if you are not satisfied after 30 days, for first-time customers with active order history. We did not open the sign-up flow, so we do not know the tax added, what happens to your card after the trial or how postage is billed.

schema_offer.description: Starter, Starter $4.99 a month (monthly billing only, up to 10 shipments a month); Growth $19.99 a month or $14 a month billed yearly (up to 100 shipments); Executive $29.99 a month or $22 a month billed yearly (unlimited shipments); Enterprise by quote; postage is paid on top of every plan. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-12.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session used the free rate calculator of Ship.com without an account. For a 2 lb box from 10001 to 94105 it showed 11 services at once, from USPS Ground Advantage at $10.15 (retail $19.80) to UPS Next Day Air Early at $103.41; a second run (60601 to 33101, 5 lb) gave UPS Ground at $11.80 as the cheapest. Only USPS and UPS appeared, and the discounts against the retail price were 11% to 80%, not the 89% of the pricing page. No surcharge was shown, although the page says UPS may charge a residential surcharge on most services. The whole test took about 2 minutes and 12 actions. The dossier says that the page shows no postage rates, which is wrong for the calculator. The plan prices are unchanged (Starter $4.99, Growth $19.99, Executive $29.99 a month). Nothing was bought and no account was made. Account and start: no account was used. Our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome on the free rate calculator at ship.com/shipping-calculator, which needs no login (the interface is in English, no cookie banner was seen). The dossier name is Ship.com and the review is on MSS (mss/ship-com-review.html). The audience tested from the dossier: Small sellers shipping up to 100 US parcels monthly. The test date is 18 Nov 2026; the start time was not recorded in the notes. Start: the heading FREE USPS AND UPS RATE CALCULATOR and under the button the line USPS and UPS prices for packages up to 70 lb within the United States. Free, no account needed. Run 1: 10001 to 94105, 2 lb, Box, 12 x 10 x 6 in (0.42 CU FT). The result came at once with 11 services: CHEAPEST OPTION $10.15 USPS Ground Advantage (That's $9.65 less than the USPS retail price; retail $19.80, Save 49%, est. delivery Wed, Nov 25); UPS Ground Saver $10.25 (2 to 7 business days, Retail price not listed); UPS Ground $10.79 (retail $28.15, Save 62%, 1 to 5 business days); USPS Priority Mail $13.91 (retail $22.55, Save 38%, est. Mon, Nov 23); UPS 3 Day Select $16.32 ($80.11, Save 80%); UPS 2nd Day Air $28.79 ($104.43, Save 72%); UPS 2nd Day Air AM $38.34 ($116.86, Save 67%); UPS Next Day Air Saver $65.79 (Fastest, $185.42, Save 65%); USPS Priority Mail Express $66.29 ($74.80, Save 11%); UPS Next Day Air $73.41 ($195.87, Save 63%); UPS Next Day Air Early $103.41 ($235.47, Save 56%). The page also names Flat Rate boxes and envelopes (6) and the notes UPS checks dimensional weight on every package. and Small and under 20 lb: it may qualify for USPS cubic pricing. Run 2: 60601 to 33101, 5 lb, 14 x 12 x 8 in (0.78 CU FT): CHEAPEST OPTION $11.80 UPS Ground (retail $24.28, Save 51%, $12.48 less than the UPS retail price); UPS Ground Saver $11.80; USPS Ground Advantage $11.81 (retail $21.00, Save 44%, est. Mon, Nov 23); UPS 3 Day Select $20.17 (Save 76%); USPS Priority Mail $23.79 (retail $29.10, Save 18%); UPS 2nd Day Air $43.44; USPS Priority Mail Express $85.37 (retail $99.70, Save 14%); UPS Next Day Air Early $110.82. No surcharge was shown. The page says that UPS may charge a residential surcharge on most services, but the calculator does not ask whether the address is residential or business. The calculator is for the United States only (up to 70 lb); international was not tested. Time: about 2 minutes and 12 actions (2 ZIP codes, the weight, 3 sizes and Calculate rates), for two runs. The discounts shown by the page itself were 11% to 80% in our two runs (USPS Ground Advantage 49% and 44%); 89% was not seen. The calculator names USPS up to 89% off and UPS up to 87% off, also without an account. Sign-up: the button Get this price (Free account, no credit card) opens /sign-up with Welcome! Let's Get Ship Done: Continue with Google, Email, First and Last name, Password, Have a code? (optional), a tick for the terms and for receiving marketing emails and SMS, and a CAPTCHA. Nothing was filled in and no label was bought; the sign-up screen was not kept as a screenshot because it shows faces of third parties. Plans: ship.com/pricing, Monthly view, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in US dollars: Starter $4.99/mo (Up to 10 Shipments/mo, One Platform Integration), Growth $19.99/mo (Up to 100 Shipments/mo, Heavily Discounted Shipping Rates), Executive $29.99/mo (Free 30-day trial, Unlimited Shipments, Up to 89% Off Shipping Rates (Lowest Rates in the US), Up to 3 Platform Integrations) and Enterprise on request (Contact us). The yearly view (Save 25%) was not looked at in the session. The FAQ says that no subscription is required to create an account and that you can compare label prices up front; you add a payment method when you are ready to print a label and buy postage. Cancelling is done in the account settings and access runs to the end of the billing period (from the FAQ). The pricing page was read again just before this delivery the same day: Monthly view Starter $4.99, Growth $19.99, Executive $29.99; Yearly view Growth $14 a month and Executive $22 a month, Starter Monthly Only; the same limits and the same line Up to 89% Off Shipping Rates; a refund of the subscription fee after 30 days for first-time customers with active order history. The prices are therefore UNCHANGED against the dossier (read 12 Nov 2026). Deviation: the dossier says that the page shows no postage rates, but the free calculator showed 11 services with postage rates without any account. Site inconsistency: an FAQ example (checked September 28, 2026) gives 1 lb from NJ to CA as USPS Ground Advantage $10.11 against $12.90 retail, while a table on the site (updated November 18, 2026) gives $8.14 against $13.65, 40% off. Cancelling: not applicable, there is no account. Not tested: an account, order import, buying a label, paying postage, the AI Shipping Manager, international rates, the residential surcharge and the yearly prices. Clean up: no account and no test data; all own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The calculator does not ask whether the address is residential or business, so the price shown may not be the final postage. UPS Ground Saver has no retail price, so no saving is shown for it. The discount against retail is 11% to 80% in our runs, not the 89% of the pricing page. Two pages of the site give different examples for the same type of parcel. The calculator is for the United States only.
